issues.reason: The Possessive / genitive NP rule routes only a "genuinely possessive of-phrase" to Possession and explicitly excludes the about / argument case ("a photo of Mary"), so (Possession sk_gamma_function_1 sk_factorial_function_1) — possessed first — asserts a possession link (the gamma function belongs to the factorial function) the sentence never states.

No rule requires a complement to sit inside the atom it modifies — every relation in this representation is a separate atom sharing a symbol — so "recoverable only by stitching two statements" describes the nominalization-argument gap the reviewer files in q2, not a false, ill-typed or over-asserted atom.

gaps_confirmed: event / result nominalization with an of-complement naming its argument ("a generalization of X", "the destruction of the city", "a photo of Mary") — the genitive rule excludes these cases but prescribes no encoding for them; only agent-nominalizations are covered
new_gaps: the entity-attached surface-preposition fallback is stated only for "from" ("wool from Calderwick"), so it is left unstated whether a leftover of-phrase may take a preposition-named (Of <entity> <entity>) atom, and whether such an atom should attach to the predicate nominal rather than the subject symbol
repair_summary: Replaced (Possession sk_gamma_function_1 sk_factorial_function_1) with the surface-preposition atom (Of sk_gamma_function_1 sk_factorial_function_1), which records the of-phrase without asserting possession; nothing else changed.
notes: Of is the preposition actually used, so it stays inside the licensed preposition-named vocabulary ("never coin a relation head"; "like …" stays the oblique (Like …)) rather than being a coined head; the atom is opaque and asserts only the stated surface relation.
